title: How to run a Black Friday sale for your app
summary: Run a Black Friday sale with the RevenueCat AI Toolkit. Set up store offers, sale paywalls, targeting, web checkout, and promotion.
body_markdown:
Black Friday is coming, and it's a good opportunity for extra sales as people are on the hunt for deals. In this guide we will go through how to run a sale for your app on App Store, Play Store, as well as web. You should be able to automate most parts of this campaign using RevenueCat CLI.


The example app I’m using in this guide is one of my own, called Netli.fyi: Netlify Client, and I’m doing two different sales for it. First one is to capture new customers by offering them a significant 50% discount on the yearly subscription. The second Black Friday campaign is to upsell existing customers by selling them a discounted lifetime plan. RevenueCat's[holiday study](https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/growth/holiday-offers-subscription-apps) found that, among apps with detected promotions, people who installed over three months earlier accounted for about half the average Black Friday increase in new paying customers.


Once Black Friday is over, I’ll update this blog post to show you how the campaign went and what I would improve.


Ready to get started? If so, begin by installing the RevenueCat CLI by following our documentation.


## Connect the AI toolkit


Install the[RevenueCat AI Toolkit plugin](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/tools/ai-toolkit/plugins) for your coding assistant. Sign in to RevenueCat. Select your project. The plugin gives your agent the skills and connection it needs to prepare store changes.


Connect the[App Store Connect API key](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/service-credentials/itunesconnect-app-specific-shared-secret/app-store-connect-api-key-configuration) and Google Play service credentials in RevenueCat first. Your account needs permission to edit products. For Google Play, the service account also needs Manage store presence.


The workflow is the same for each store: ask for a plan, review the changes, then approve the exact plan. The manual steps below are fallbacks.


For terminal work, install and sign in to the RevenueCat CLI too:


```text
brew   install   RevenueCat/tap/rc
rc   auth   login
rc   projects   use
rc   auth   status
```


## Step 1: Prepare the App Store offer


Netli.fyi’s yearly offer reduces the first payment from $24.99 to $12.49. Renewals stay at $24.99 per year. The sale runs from November 25 through December 1, 2026, with regular offers returning on December 2.


Ask your agent to inspect the existing subscription before it prepares the change. Include the app, product, dates, and regional pricing rule in your prompt:


```text
Use the RevenueCat AI Toolkit to prepare Netli.fyi’s App Store sale.
Inspect the existing yearly subscription and introductory offers first.
Offer 50% off the first year from November 25 through December 1, 2026.
Return to regular offers on December 2. Keep renewal prices unchanged.
Use each storefront’s regular price to calculate its discount.
Account for the current trial and explain when to schedule its return.
Show the Product Editor plan and review link before changing the store.
If the sale is already configured, report that instead of duplicating it.
```


### Review the plan before applying it


Open the[Product Editor](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/offerings/product-editor-configure) review link from the agent. Check the subscription, offer duration, dates, and regional prices. A $24.99 yearly plan should show a first-year price near $12.49. Check each currency against its regular price.


Resolve blocking warnings before you approve the plan. Then ask the agent to apply that exact plan. A new plan can contain different changes, so do not recreate it between review and approval. Check the result in App Store Connect after it completes.


Review the offer dates and payment period. This US example uses an unapplied plan for the development app.Check the first-year price before you select Commit to store. The development example has not been applied.


An introductory offer is available once per customer in a subscription group. A previous trial counts. Customers who are not eligible need a different offer, such as an offer code.


### Manual fallback: App Store Connect


Open Subscriptions → subscription group → yearly subscription → Subscription Prices → View all Subscription Pricing.


End the current trial when the sale starts. Choose Set up Introductory Offer. Select the storefronts. Set the sale dates. Choose Pay up front. Set the duration to one year. Enter the regional offer prices. Check the schedule before you confirm it.


A trial followed by the scheduled first-year discount in App Store Connect.


Add the trial’s return to your calendar. Apple permits[one current and one future introductory offer](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/set-up-introductory-offers-for-auto-renewable-subscriptions/) per storefront. Once the sale starts in all selected storefronts, schedule the trial to return when the sale ends. It does not restart automatically.


### Include former subscribers and lifetime buyers


For former subscribers, create a[subscription offer code](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-subscriptions/set-up-subscription-offer-codes) in the subscription’s pricing settings. Select the eligible customer types and discounted terms. Prepare the offer before launch, then create the custom code when redemption should start.


Netli.fyi’s lifetime offer reduces $99.99 to $49.99. Ask the agent for a separate price plan for the non-consumable product. Review both the sale price and the return to regular pricing. You can also set these in In-App Purchases → lifetime product → Price Schedule.


## Step 2: Prepare the Google Play offer


Use the same discount on your existing auto-renewing yearly base plan. Google Play keeps the base plan’s renewal price and puts the first-year discount in a separate offer:


```text
Use the RevenueCat AI Toolkit to prepare Netli.fyi’s Google Play sale.
Inspect the existing yearly base plan, trial, and sale offer first.
Prepare 50% off the first year for eligible new customers.
Keep the base plan’s renewal prices unchanged.
Use a one-year single-payment phase and check regional discounts.
Show the review plan before applying changes.
List the activation and deactivation steps for November 25 and December 2.
Do not activate the offer or disable the trial yet.
```


Review the product, base plan, eligibility, payment phase, and regional prices before applying the plan. Google Play offers do not have the same date scheduling as App Store introductory offers. Prepare the offer in advance, then activate and deactivate it at the sale boundaries.


With RevenueCat’s[automatic offer selection](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/subscription-guidance/subscription-offers) , an eligible free trial takes priority over a discount. Deactivate the trial when you activate the sale offer. Keep the base plan active. At the end, deactivate the discount and activate the trial again.


### Manual fallback: Google Play Console


Open Monetize with Play → Products → Subscriptions. Select the yearly subscription and choose Add offer under Base plans and offers.


Enter an offer ID such as bf-2026. Choose New customer acquisition. Select the purchase-history restriction. Add a Single payment phase for one year or 12 months. Set a 50% percentage discount. Check the regional prices before you save.


A one-year payment phase with 50% regional discounts in Play Console.


If your app selects SubscriptionOptions directly, select the sale option in that code. A campaign tag alone does not select it. For lifetime access, use a non-consumable one-time product. If your purchase code does not support one-time discount offers, change its base price at the sale boundaries.


## Step 3: Connect the web offer


A Web Purchase Link gives you a hosted paywall and checkout to share from your sale page, email, or social posts. Netli.fyi uses Paddle. If you use[RevenueCat Billing](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/web/web-billing/product-setup) or[Stripe Billing](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/web/integrations/stripe) , follow the provider’s setup guide instead.


Use the toolkit to check the RevenueCat product mapping, entitlement, and Offering. It does not create Paddle products, prices, or discounts. Set those up in Paddle, then create the Web Purchase Link in the RevenueCat dashboard:


```text
Inspect the web Offering and premium entitlement in RevenueCat.
Check that the Paddle yearly product unlocks the same access as mobile.
List the RevenueCat settings needed for a Web Purchase Link.
Show which settings belong in Paddle and which belong in RevenueCat.
Check the App User ID and purchase redemption flow.
Show the proposed changes before applying them.
```


### Set the web price and checkout


Connect Paddle using the[integration guide](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/web/integrations/paddle) . For Web Purchase Links, Paddle must approve pay.rev.cat. Check the guide’s default payment link and checkout settings.


In Paddle, create the yearly price and a 50% discount for its first payment. Restrict the discount to that price. Set the BLACKFRIDAY code and expiry. Renewals keep the regular price.


Import the price into RevenueCat. Attach it to the premium entitlement your app checks. Add it to a yearly package in a web Offering. In Funnels → Purchase Links, create the link with that Offering and your Paddle configuration.


Show the first charge and renewal terms. Enable discount entry in Paddle and RevenueCat’s Paddle configuration. Tell customers to enter BLACKFRIDAY at checkout.


The saved purchase link connects the yearly Offering to Paddle and explains the discount code.


### Connect the payment to the app user


For an identified purchase, use the Share URL format with the customer’s URL-encoded App User ID. Use the same ID in your mobile app. For purchases before sign-in, configure[Redemption Links](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/web/redemption-links) and release the required app support first.


Pass the App User ID at checkout, or redeem the purchase in the app.


Test the link with a separate Paddle sandbox account. Check the discount, renewal price, and premium access in the app before sharing the production URL.


## Step 4: Build the sale paywalls


Ask the agent to duplicate your current paywall so the sale keeps your app’s design. Use one Offering for yearly and one for lifetime. Both sets of products must unlock the same premium entitlement.


Give the agent your app’s design files and a screenshot. For the yearly paywall, use this prompt:


```text
Use the RevenueCat AI Toolkit to duplicate my current yearly paywall.
Use my app’s design files and screenshot as the design reference.
Attach the duplicate to the Black Friday yearly Offering.
Show 50% off the first year only when the customer is eligible.
Use localized price variables and show the full renewal terms.
Keep Restore purchases, Terms, and Privacy links.
Show the draft and a preview for review. Do not publish it yet.
```


For lifetime, use a separate Offering and ask for a one-time payment design. Explain that buying lifetime does not cancel the yearly subscription. Add a button to manage that subscription after purchase.


The yearly sale design with introductory-offer rules. The builder uses sample prices and durations in this preview.The lifetime sale design explains yearly renewal management. The preview uses a sample price.


### Review the paywalls and schedule targeting


Review both paywalls before publishing them. Then ask the agent to prepare the targeting rule. Use exact UTC times that match the store offers:


```text
Use the RevenueCat AI Toolkit to prepare the Black Friday targeting rule.
Route customers with no active entitlement to the yearly sale Offering.
Include onboarding and the other placements where I show a paywall.
Start November 25, 2026 at 08:00 UTC.
End December 2, 2026 at 08:00 UTC.
Put the rule above broader rules that would otherwise match.
Show the audience, placements, times, and priority before saving.
After I approve, publish the reviewed paywall and save the scheduled rule.
```


Check the audience, Offering, placements, UTC times, and rule priority before you approve the rule.[Targeting requires a Pro or Enterprise plan](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/tools/targeting) . It controls which paywall appears; it does not set the store price or decide store-offer eligibility.


For lifetime, add an entry point for your selected yearly subscribers. Hide it from lifetime owners. Release any required app update before the sale.


Audience example: Has active entitlement is False excludes customers who already have access. This is an unsaved editor preview.


### Test the full purchase


Use a test App User ID to preview the Offering. This checks configuration, not payment. Clear the override after the test:


```text
rc   customers   override-offering   your_test_user   --offering   ofrng_your_sale
rc   offerings   preview   app_your_ios   --app-user-id   your_test_user   --json
rc   offerings   preview   app_your_android   --app-user-id   your_test_user   --json
rc   customers   clear-override   your_test_user
```


Complete sandbox purchases on iOS and Android. On Android, use a Google Play build and a license tester. Check eligible and ineligible yearly offers, the lifetime entitlement, and the button to manage yearly renewals.


## Step 5: Tell customers about the sale


Prepare the promotion before launch, but send it after you have checked the sale prices and purchase flow. Give new customers the yearly offer. Give eligible yearly subscribers the lifetime offer. Exclude lifetime owners from messages that sell access they already have.


Publish a sale page with the price, eligibility, renewal terms, and end time. Link to the correct purchase flow for each platform.


The sale page shows both offers, their audiences, and the renewal terms.


Send an email or push notification to customers you can contact for marketing. Link directly to the sale paywall or web checkout. Test the link on a phone, including when the app is closed. Follow the consent and unsubscribe rules that apply to your audience.


Plan one reminder near the end. For Netli.fyi’s November 25–December 1 campaign, the Cyber Monday message can say the sale ends tomorrow. State the exact deadline so customers know which time zone applies.


### End the sale and review the results


Restore the trial and regular lifetime prices. End the targeting rule and web discount, then update the sale page. Test old campaign links to confirm that they show the regular offer.


Compare new yearly customers with a period before the sale. Count lifetime purchases separately. Keep the promotion links and campaign dates with the results so you can compare the next sale.


## Wrap up


In this guide we’ve gone through how to run a Black Friday sale for your app on the web, App Store, and Play Store.
